Folks — forwarding Hannah's note. Can you help map a defensible initial set of offers for AWS and call out differences for GCP/Azure? High level thinking below. I've attached a working matrix (redwood-offer-matrix-v1.xlsx).

Proposed initial SKU constructs (draft):
- hosted-api-standard (metered token consumption, monthly subscription fallback)
- hosted-api-pro (higher RPS TTL + SLOs, subscription + metered)
- dedicated-commit-1x (1x reserved GPU pool; subscription annual)
- dedicated-commit-4x (4x pool, enterprise pricing)
- private-vpc-essentials (VPC connector + private control plane; enterprise-only offer)

Regional guidance (draft):
- US & EU: list hosted + dedicated + private (where contractual controls exist)
- APAC: soft launch for hosted only (cost + compliance checks)
- GCP: prefer containerized/billed usage or marketplace SaaS with usage-reporting — start with hosted-api-standard in us-central
- Azure: enterprise offer model is different; likely need a separate SKU for Azure Enterprise Agreement customers.

Open asks: pricing granularity per-region, minimum billing unit (token vs. request), and whether we want separate SKUs for quantized/quantized-optimized model variants.

Next step: can one of you pull the compliance/packaging constraints and I'll schedule a sync with Hannah + Sara (GCP) + Simon (Azure) for early next week.

Thanks — Ben

Ben / Marissa — quick notes from product/ops perspective: 

1) Marketplace offer model constraints
- AWS & Azure: subscription + metered is straightforward; AWS supports AMI / SaaS listings; for Dedicated (reserved GPU) we should model as subscription with usage tiers and an explicit "commit" SKU.
- GCP: tends to prefer containerized or SaaS with usage integration — pricing needs to map cleanly to their billing APIs.

2) Region gating and staged rollout
- Start with US + EU for full set (hosted + dedicated). EU requires explicit data residency notes and updated DPA language on the listing.
- APAC: hold for Q3 pilot; require legal/regional sales alignment first.

3) Co-sell qualification and artifacts
- Need SOC2 Type II evidence (we have it), basic usage metrics (3 months), reference customer contact, and a documented partner success plan.

4) SKU naming & compatibility
- Suggest canonical SKU names in matrix. Avoid embedding region in SKU (keep SKU stable across regions) and instead use offer-level region availability to reduce churn when we add regions. That helps co-sell reporting.

I'll annotate the spreadsheet with model compatibility notes and the minimal tech checklist (billing APIs, SCIM for SSO where required, onboarding automation).

Jonas
Director, Product Ops
